intro.author: Traditionally Moses, receiving God's words at the tabernacle (1:1). Many scholars attribute the book to Israel's priestly circles and date its final form later.
intro.written: Traditionally during Israel's year at Mount Sinai; many scholars date its final shaping to the time of the kings or the exile.
intro.audience: Israel's priests and people, learning how to live with a holy God in their midst
intro.setting: Exodus ends with God's glory filling the new tabernacle. Leviticus picks up immediately, with Israel still camped at Sinai, as God speaks from that tent about sacrifice, priesthood, purity and holy living. The name comes from the Levites, Israel's priestly tribe.
intro.purpose: To show how sinful people can approach and live near a holy God, through sacrifice, priests, purity and everyday obedience.
intro.bigIdea: Be holy, because the LORD your God is holy.
